minutes.headline: Select Board ratified two town hires, set the town manager's self-evaluation deadline, and reviewed the Shady Point license.
minutes.summary: Outgoing member Alonzo held his last meeting; the board was thanked with a plaque from residents and heard the water district's complaint over the PFAS vote. It ratified two appointments, approved the existing manager evaluation form, set a deadline for the manager's self-evaluation, and reviewed edits to the Shady Point boat access license. The annual election with an override question on the ballot was announced, with no budget figures set out.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-0 to ratify the town manager's appointments of a police public safety coordinator and a public access videographer.
The board unanimously approved the existing town manager evaluation form, then voted 4-0 to set May 26 as the deadline for the manager's self-evaluation.
The evaluation schedule runs through member meetings the week of June 3, a first presentation on June 18 and a vote on June 25.
A decision on the surplus property policy was deferred a week so department heads could give feedback.
The board reviewed edits to the Shady Point boat access license without voting, and heard the water district's complaint over the PFAS vote with no action.

why_it_matters: The annual election will carry an override question, which if approved is added to the tax rolls permanently and shared by town households, so it touches every tax bill.
The surplus property policy and the Shady Point license are unfinished, so rules for selling town property and for public boat access are still open.
watch_next: The surplus property policy decision, deferred to next Tuesday.
The town manager evaluation: first presentation June 18 and board vote June 25.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the three clear votes (two ratified appointments and the evaluation form) and on the $10,000 warrant. They differ on the evaluation timeline: ours records a dated schedule and a May 26 deadline vote, while the official minutes record an undated timeline motion with no tally. The official minutes also carry the plaque, the tax report item and the public commenters, and omit the water district figures and the town meeting policy decision.
